name: @torque-labs/mcp

tools.name: auth
tools.description: Manage Torque authentication with a browser-approved device code. Use login to receive a verification URL and user code, approve it in the browser, then call complete to perform one token check. Use status to inspect/revalidate the current session and logout to revoke a locally managed session. TORQUE_SESSION_TOKEN remains an optional externally managed bootstrap and is never persisted.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated

List all Torque projects accessible to the signed-in account and mark which is currently active.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- Immediately after authentication succeeds, to surface available projects
- The user wants to switch projects or needs an ID for `set_active_project`
- Verifying which project is currently active

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Changing the active project — use `set_active_project` instead

tools.name: set_active_project
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated

Validate a project ID and set it as active for subsequent project-scoped operations. If the user does not know the ID, call `list_projects` first and wait for them to choose.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- The user supplies or chooses a specific project ID

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Discovering project IDs — use `list_projects` first
- Viewing project metadata — use `list_projects` or `get_ai_context` instead

projectId.description: The project ID to validate and set as active. Use `list_projects` to find it.

tools.name: get_ai_context
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`

Fetch the active project's AI context. Without arguments it returns the project's token/program addresses and an index of its context files (name, size, topics); with `files` it returns those files in full. Cached per project for the session.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- Starting any incentive-creation flow, to ground parameter choices in project context
- Interpreting tool results that reference project-specific programs or domain terms
- Read the index first, then open the files that match the question with `files`. Project-specific notes (metrics, crates, rules) are often in a file named after the project.

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Listing projects — use `list_projects` instead
- Changing the active project — use `set_active_project` instead
- Naming the project's tokens, their decimals or USD prices — use `get_tokens`

files.description: File names from the index that a call without arguments returns. Returns those files in full.

tools.name: get_tokens
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`

List the active project's token and program addresses, with each token's symbol, name, decimals and USD price. Pass `mints` to name other tokens too. Returns no project notes.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- Naming a token or mint that a tool result or the user mentions, or saying whether it is one of the project's tokens
- Converting a base-unit amount with the token's decimals, or a token amount to USD at today's price

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Project notes or context files — use `get_ai_context`
- USD amounts a tool already reports — use that tool's value

mints.description: Up to 20 more token mint addresses to name, such as a reward mint another tool returned.

tools.name: reset_context
tools.description:
Clear the active project and the AI-context cache. Authentication state is left unchanged.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- The user wants to start fresh without re-authenticating
- Switching focus to a different project and want a clean slate

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Signing out — use `auth({ action: "logout" })` instead
- Switching to a specific project — use `set_active_project` instead (the AI-context cache clears on project change)

tools.name: list_incentives
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`

List incentives on the active project. Returns incentive IDs, payout types, status, active epoch, and escrow state. Use an ID from this tool with `get_incentive`. The incentive status and the epoch status are separate: an incentive can be DRAFT while its epoch is EVALUATING, so judge whether a campaign is running by its active epoch, and do not filter with `isActive` when the user wants every campaign.

isActive.description: Filter to active or non-active incentives.

tools.name: get_incentive
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`
- data: `incentiveId` — call `list_incentives` first

Get the complete configuration for one incentive, including its qualification query's SQL or DSL spec (the rule for who qualifies and how wallets score), distribution settings, epochs (number, status, and evaluation window, for `get_incentive_leaderboard`'s `epoch`), schedule, and funding/emitter state. Its epoch ids are the `epochId` for `get_metrics`, `run_query` and `get_incentive_analytics` (emissions view).

tools.name: get_incentive_leaderboard
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`
- data: `incentiveId` — call `list_incentives` first

Get the per-wallet leaderboard for an incentive: the live board, one epoch's board, or the board at a past time. Omit `epoch` and `asOf` for the live board (the latest run). Pass `epoch` (an epoch number from `get_incentive`) for one epoch's board: its final run once the epoch has finished, for example "week 1 final board". Pass `epoch` and `asOf` for that epoch's board at a past time. The output states which board was read (live, final run, or snapshot run and its time). Returns one bounded page with every result column produced by the incentive query; use the returned cursor, with the same `epoch` and `asOf`, for the next page. For totals, counts, shares, or concentration over the whole board, pass `totals: true` instead of paging and adding rows. For figures over time, such as the Gini coefficient at the end of each day of an epoch, call once per day with `epoch`, `asOf`, and `totals: true`, and quote each result.

epoch.description: The epoch number to read (from `get_incentive`). Returns that epoch's final run once it has finished, else its latest run. Omit for the live board.

asOf.description: ISO 8601 time, for example 2026-09-24T23:59:59Z. Reads the board as it stood then: only runs created at or before this time count. Combine with `epoch` for a snapshot during that epoch.

totals.description: true to read the whole board in one request (up to 10,000 rows) and return its first `limit` rows with the ranked-wallet count, the sum of the ranked measure, top-N shares, the Gini coefficient, and the score at each prize-tier boundary. Use it for each participant's standing, the sum over participants and the number of ranked wallets, and for concentration, instead of adding rows yourself. Not with `cursor`. For raw measures such as volume use `run_query`.

tools.name: get_incentive_analytics
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`
- data: `incentiveId` — call `list_incentives` first
- data: `epochId` — call `get_incentive` first (emissions view only)

Read fixed incentive facts from the platform: funded, allocated, claimed, and balance per payout token (summary); one row per epoch with emission and claim counts and windows (epochs); the per-wallet allocation rows of one epoch (emissions, paged); or the escrow funding events (funding, paged); or a crate incentive's crates earned, opened and claimed, spend per token, and stock left per crate type (crates).

[USE THIS WHEN]
- One incentive's funded, allocated and claimed amounts to date, its epochs, emissions, funding events and crate counts

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Rewards counted in a window, per incentive, with their cost — use `get_rewards`
- An incentive's own ranking or scores — use `get_incentive_leaderboard`
- A public incentive another project owns — read it with `get_incentive` and `get_incentive_leaderboard`

view.description: summary: funded, allocated, claimed, and balance per payout token. epochs: one row per epoch with counts and windows. emissions: per-wallet allocation rows of one epoch (needs epochId). funding: escrow funding events. crates: a crate incentive's crates — earned (allocated), opened (opening one creates its emission), claimed, spend per token in each token's own units, and the stock left per crate type.

epochId.description: Epoch id from `get_incentive`; required for the emissions view.

limit.description: Page size for emissions and funding, 1..200 (default 50).

cursor.description: The nextCursor of a previous page, to read the next one.

tools.name: get_rewards
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`

Rewards the active project's own incentives count for one window, in USDC: an epoch incentive (leaderboards and other per-epoch payouts) at what its finalized epochs allocated, in the window each epoch ends in; a milestone incentive (crates, thresholds) at distributed (claimed) USDC to date, in the window it starts in. Lists accruing and pending epochs, incentives granted from another project, and payouts in other tokens without counting them. Pass `volumeUsd` for cost in basis points on each line and in total.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- Rewards counted in a window, per incentive, with their cost: the whole project, one line each — read the line for the incentive asked about

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Volume or traders — use `get_metrics` or `run_query`
- One incentive's funded, allocated and claimed amounts to date, its epochs, emissions, funding events and crate counts — use `get_incentive_analytics`

from.description: Window start, an ISO instant (inclusive), e.g. 2026-09-23T17:00:00Z.

volumeUsd.description: Optional volume in USD for the same window; adds a bps column.

tools.name: get_metrics
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`
- data: `incentiveId` — call `list_incentives` first (optional)
- data: `epochId` — call `get_incentive` first (optional)

List the project's saved metrics (named DSL queries that each return one number), with what each reads, which an incentive has attached, and their current values on that incentive. Check here before writing a new query: a saved metric may already answer the question. A metric's value covers the incentive's whole window or one epoch; for any other window, run its `spec` from `get_metrics` with `run_query` and `start`/`end`. When you report a metric, name what it reads (its Reads column) and its window.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- Any question about a project's or incentive's numbers — check for a saved metric first
- The user asks what metrics exist, which are attached, or how they are doing
- Before `save_metric`, to avoid a duplicate

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Numbers no saved metric covers — write a spec and use `run_query`
- An incentive's own ranking or scores — use `get_incentive_leaderboard`
- One incentive's funded, allocated and claimed amounts to date, its epochs, emissions, funding events and crate counts — use `get_incentive_analytics`
- Rewards counted in a window, per incentive, with their cost — use `get_rewards`

incentiveId.description: Incentive id from `list_incentives`, to mark the metrics it has attached.

values.description: Read each attached metric's value for the incentive (needs incentiveId), over its window or one epoch.

epochId.description: Epoch id from `get_incentive`: read values for that epoch only.

tools.name: get_dsl_guide
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`
- data: `incentiveId` — call `list_incentives` first (optional)

Read how to write a Torque DSL query (a JSON spec, never SQL): the rules, the catalog of tables and fields, worked examples, the metric rules, or the exact spec schema. Read the default (overview + metrics) and the catalog before writing your first spec in a session.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- Before writing a spec for `run_query` or `save_metric`
- A spec failed validation and you need the rules, the fields or an example

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Answering the data question — run the spec with `run_query`
- Listing saved metrics — use `get_metrics`

section.description: overview: how to write a spec. catalog: every table, field, operator and aggregate fn you may use, plus the project's events. examples: valid specs to copy. metrics: the metric rules. schema: the spec's JSON Schema, which says what each key does and which values it takes (large — read it to look up a key or value, or when a spec keeps failing). Omit for overview + metrics.

incentiveId.description: Incentive id from `list_incentives` (one this project owns): the catalog and examples for that incentive, including the examples that read only its participants.

tools.name: run_query
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`
- data: `spec` — call `get_dsl_guide` first (read the guide and catalog first)
- data: `incentiveId` — call `list_incentives` first (optional)

Validate and run a Torque DSL spec on the project or one of its own incentives (`accessSource: OWNER`), and return the rows, the window read, and whether the result can be saved as a metric. Torque checks the spec, scopes it to the project and runs it; nothing is saved.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- A question about volume, traders, counts, events, trends, breakdowns or top wallets by a raw measure (such as volume) that no saved metric covers, for the project or one incentive
- A saved metric over a window other than its incentive's or epoch's: run its `spec` from `get_metrics` with `start`/`end`
- An incentive's volume, traders or split: pass `incentiveId` (`population` says when to read only its participants)
- Checking a spec before `save_metric`

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- A saved metric over its incentive's window or one epoch — read it with `get_metrics`
- An incentive's own ranking or scores — use `get_incentive_leaderboard` (`totals: true` gives each participant's standing, the sum over participants and the number of ranked wallets)
- One incentive's funded, allocated and claimed amounts to date, its epochs, emissions, funding events and crate counts — use `get_incentive_analytics`
- Rewards counted in a window, per incentive, with their cost — use `get_rewards`
- An incentive another project owns — a granted one with `get_incentive_analytics`, a public one with `get_incentive`; its ranking as above
- SQL — the DSL is the only query language here

spec.description: The Torque DSL spec, a JSON object — never SQL. The tables and fields, and what each field means, are `get_dsl_guide` section "catalog"; patterns to copy are section "examples"; section "schema" says what each key does and which values it takes (large — read it to look up a key or value, or when a spec keeps failing). Never paste wallet addresses from another tool into a filter. Keep a read to an incentive's ranked users with `population: "participants"`, or to the wallets it rewarded with an `existsIn` on its rewards table (catalog). Ask the user first: which events link a user's wallets before rolling them into one person with an `identity`, and which pattern and span before a wash-trade check on the source's own table (`get_dsl_guide`).

incentiveId.description: Run on this incentive: without dates it reads the incentive's own window (its epochs, or a milestone's dates), up to now while it runs.

epochId.description: Epoch id from `get_incentive` (needs incentiveId): read that epoch's window.

start.description: Window start: an ISO 8601 datetime, or a date (UTC midnight). Omit to read the incentive's own window (its epochs, or a milestone's dates), up to now while it runs, or the last 30 days at project level.

end.description: Window end, excluded: an ISO 8601 datetime, or a date (UTC midnight). Defaults to now; needs start.

population.description: Needs incentiveId. Omit it, or pass `market`, to run the spec as written: every wallet its filters match on the incentive's targets. `participants`: only the users its board ranks; the API adds that filter, returns the spec it ran, and gives a reason instead of rows when no one is ranked. Use it when the user asks about the incentive's participants or leaderboard users.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated

Preview and create a Torque project. First call with `confirmed: false`; repeat the exact input with the returned confirmation token after explicit approval. The new project becomes active unless `makeActive` is false.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- The user wants to start a new Torque project

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Switching between existing projects — use `set_active_project` instead
- Listing existing projects — use `list_projects` instead

tools.name: save_metric
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`
- data: `spec` — call `run_query` first (run it first)
- data: `metricId` — call `get_metrics` first
- data: `incentiveIds` — call `list_incentives` first

Save a DSL query as a metric (one number each incentive reads over its own window) and attach it to incentives, or attach an existing metric. First call previews: it checks for a duplicate, runs the query, and returns a confirmation token. After the user approves, repeat the exact input with `confirmed: true` and the token. Attaching adds the metric and keeps the incentive's others.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- `run_query` said a result is metric-ready and the user wants to keep tracking it
- The user asks to create a metric, or to add an existing metric to incentives

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Running a query without saving — use `run_query`
- Reading metric values — use `get_metrics`
- Renaming, editing or deleting a metric — not possible here. Tell the user to do it on the platform, and give the metric's `platformUrl` from `get_metrics`

name.description: The new metric's name, 1–64 characters, unique in the project. Create only.

description.description: One sentence on what the number counts. Create only.

spec.description: The Torque DSL spec, a JSON object — never SQL. The tables and fields, and what each field means, are `get_dsl_guide` section "catalog"; patterns to copy are section "examples"; section "schema" says what each key does and which values it takes (large — read it to look up a key or value, or when a spec keeps failing). A metric's spec returns one row with one number. Create only; run it with `run_query` first.

metricId.description: A metric from `get_metrics` to attach. Attach only.

incentiveIds.description: Incentives this project owns (`accessSource: OWNER` in `list_incentives`) to attach the metric to. Attaching keeps their other metrics. Required to attach an existing metric.

tools.name: save_dsl_query
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`
- data: `spec` — call `run_query` first (run it first)

Save a DSL spec as a named query of the project, so it can be reused or back an incentive. First call previews: it runs the spec once and returns a confirmation token. After the user approves, repeat the exact input with `confirmed: true` and the token.

[USE THIS WHEN]
- The user wants to keep a query they ran for reuse
- An incentive should run a saved query, passed as `dslQueryId` to `create_incentive`

[DO NOT USE FOR]
- Saving a number to track — use `save_metric`
- Running a query without saving it — use `run_query`

description.description: One sentence on what the query counts.

spec.description: The Torque DSL spec, a JSON object — never SQL. The tables and fields are `get_dsl_guide` section "catalog"; patterns to copy are section "examples"; section "schema" says what each key does and which values it takes (large — read it to look up a key or value, or when a spec keeps failing). Run it with `run_query` first.

tools.name: create_incentive
tools.description:
[PREREQUISITES]
- session: authenticated, active project set via `set_active_project`
- data: `spec` — call `run_query` first (run it first)
- data: `dslQueryId` — call `save_dsl_query` first

Preview and create a Torque incentive that runs a DSL query each epoch, or on a milestone's cadence: a saved `dslQueryId`, or a `spec` saved as a DSL query on confirm. Never SQL. First call without `confirmed`; after the user explicitly approves the exact preview, repeat the same inputs with the returned `confirmationToken` and `confirmed: true`. This creates configuration only; funding remains a separate platform action.

[PAYOUT TYPES]
- EXACT: Pays each wallet its metric as the amount, largest first, until the pool runs out. Fits when the query already works out each wallet's reward. distributionConfig: EXACT paying tokens.
- LEADERBOARD: Ranks wallets by their metric, highest first, and pays each rank a set prize. Fits a competition, such as the top traders by volume. distributionConfig: LEADERBOARD paying tokens, or LEADERBOARD paying crates (rewardKind "CRATE").
- REBATE: Pays each wallet a percent of its metric, in one token. Fits cashback on volume or fees. distributionConfig: REBATE paying tokens.
- RAFFLE: Draws winners for set prizes. WEIGHTED_BY_METRIC uses the metric as tickets; EQUAL_CHANCES ignores it. Fits a draw among everyone who qualifies. distributionConfig: RAFFLE paying tokens, or RAFFLE paying crates (rewardKind "CRATE").
- FIXED: Pays every wallet the query returns the same reward and ignores the metric. Fits a flat reward for doing something, such as a first trade. distributionConfig: FIXED paying tokens, or FIXED paying crates (rewardKind "CRATE").
The metric is any number column the query returns: volume, trade count, fees, a computed score.
A MILESTONE is an incentive kind, not a payout type: it pays FIXED tokens, or crates (rewardKind "CRATE") under LEADERBOARD, RAFFLE or FIXED.

name.description: The incentive's name, shown to its participants.

description.description: What the incentive rewards, shown to its participants.

startDate.description: When the incentive starts, an ISO 8601 datetime. Omit to leave it an unscheduled draft.

endDate.description: When the incentive ends, an ISO 8601 datetime after `startDate`. Omit for no end.

addressColumn.description: The output column holding each paid wallet. Defaults to the spec's `account`.

metricColumn.description: The output column holding each wallet's metric: any number the query returns, such as volume, trade count, fees or a computed score. Defaults to the spec's `score`. LEADERBOARD ranks by it, REBATE pays a percent of it, EXACT pays it as the amount, and a WEIGHTED_BY_METRIC RAFFLE uses it as tickets; FIXED and an EQUAL_CHANCES RAFFLE ignore it.

evalDurationSeconds.description: Each epoch's length in seconds. The API asks for it on a MILESTONE too.

claimDurationSeconds.description: How long rewards stay claimable, in seconds. The API's default is 86400 (one day).

evalQueryFrequency.description: Seconds between query runs while an epoch is live. A MILESTONE runs on `milestoneCadence` instead.

requiresKyc.description: Whether a wallet must pass KYC before it can claim. The API's default is false.

reviewLevel.description: MANUAL: each epoch's results wait as an editable list until the owner signs them off on the platform, and only then is anything paid. OFF, the API's default: results are paid as worked out. A MILESTONE cannot be held for review.

kind.description: The incentive kind, not a payout type. EPOCH, the API's default: payouts are worked out once, when each epoch ends. MILESTONE: a wallet is paid the moment the query first returns it, checked on `milestoneCadence`; it pays FIXED tokens, or crates under LEADERBOARD, RAFFLE or FIXED. The API refuses a MILESTONE paying tokens on any other payout type, or one that sets `claimStartTimeOfDay` or a POOL_PERCENTAGE ladder, or is held for review.

milestoneCadence.description: How often a MILESTONE checks its query: MINUTE (every 5 minutes), HOURLY or DAILY. Required for a MILESTONE, and refused for an EPOCH incentive.

metricIds.description: Saved metrics the incentive shows, by id from `get_metrics`, at most 4.

targetMints.description: The tokens the incentive is about, by mint (`get_tokens` lists the project's). They fill the token filters of the metrics and widgets on this incentive, not who is paid. A metric that leaves that filter for the incentive to fill reads nothing until it is set; a metric that names its own values ignores it.

targetMarkets.description: The perps markets the incentive is about, by market symbol such as SOL (the guide catalog's market field lists them). They fill the market filters of the metrics and widgets on this incentive, not who is paid. A metric that leaves that filter for the incentive to fill reads nothing until it is set; a metric that names its own values ignores it.

targetAttributions.description: The apps whose routed trades the incentive counts, by the name the trades carry; "" means trades no app routed. They fill the app filters of the metrics and widgets on this incentive, not who is paid. Left empty, a metric that leaves that filter for the incentive counts every app; a metric that names its own apps ignores it.

dslQueryId.description: A saved DSL query (from `save_dsl_query`) for the incentive to run. Pass this or `spec`.

spec.description: A Torque DSL spec, a JSON object — never SQL, saved as a new DSL query on confirm. Pass this or `dslQueryId`. It returns one row per wallet: set `account` to the wallet column and, for a payout that reads a metric, `score` to the metric column (any number column: volume, trade count, fees, a computed score). Give it a `timeWindow` with `startParam: "startDate"` and `endParam: "endDate"`, which each run fills with the window it reads. Its only params can be that window (`startDate`, `endDate`) and the ids each run fills in for the incentive; the API refuses any other. The tables and fields are `get_dsl_guide` section "catalog"; section "schema" says what each key does and which values it takes (large — read it to look up a key or value, or when a spec keeps failing). Run it with `run_query` first.

queryDescription.description: With `spec`: one sentence on what the query counts, saved with it.

image.description: An image URL shown with the incentive.

payoutType.description: EXACT, LEADERBOARD, REBATE, RAFFLE or FIXED; this tool's description says what each does.

tokenAddress.description: The token's mint address (`get_tokens` lists them).

uiAmount.description: The amount in whole tokens as a decimal string, such as "1000" or "2.5" — never base units.

totalFundAmount.description: The pool it pays from, per epoch on an EPOCH incentive: one token leg per token, each amount above 0. Each wallet is paid its metric in every token listed.

rewardKind.description: Optional "DIRECT": the payout pays tokens. Leaving it out means the same.

maxPerParticipant.description: A cap, a decimal string above 0: the most of each token one wallet is paid (per epoch on an EPOCH incentive). On a RAFFLE paying tokens, the most tickets one wallet holds.

distributionMethod.description: Always "CLAIM": each wallet claims its reward on the platform.

timezoneOffset.description: Hours from UTC, -12 to 14, that `claimStartTimeOfDay` is read in.

claimStartTimeOfDay.description: EPOCH only. A time of day as "HH:MM" (24-hour). Claims open at the next such time after an epoch ends; without it they open when the epoch ends.

anyOf.description: EXACT paying tokens: a pool and an optional cap per wallet.

totalFundAmount.description: The pool it pays from, per epoch on an EPOCH incentive: one token leg per token, each amount above 0. Every token a rank pays needs a pool here, and every pool here must be one of the tokens it pays.

rewardKind.description: Optional "DIRECT": the payout pays tokens. Leaving it out means the same.

valueType.description: How a rank's `value` amounts read. "ALLOCATION": paid as written, and a token's ranks may total no more than its pool. "POOL_PERCENTAGE": each amount is the percent of that token's pool the rank gets, and a token's percents total 100 or less.

uiAmount.description: The amount in whole tokens as a decimal string, such as "1000" or "2.5" — never base units.

manualRanks.description: The prize ladder. Wallets rank by the metric, highest first, so rank 1 is the top. A row is `{rank, value}` for one rank or `{rankFrom, rankTo, value}` for a range (rankTo at least rankFrom), never both. A rank can be in only one row. `value` is a list of token legs: what each wallet at that rank is paid.

anyOf.description: LEADERBOARD paying tokens: a pool, how rank values read, and the prize ladder.

rewardKind.description: "CRATE": the payout pays crates instead of tokens.

crateInventory.description: The crate types. Each `{count, legs}` means `count` crates exist (at least 1 on a new incentive), each opening to `legs`, a list of token legs. Which type a crate is gets drawn when it is opened.

anyOf.description: LEADERBOARD paying crates (rewardKind "CRATE"): every wallet the query returns earns one crate while stock lasts, drawn from `crateInventory`; the LEADERBOARD fields for tokens are not used.

totalFundAmount.description: The pool it pays from, per epoch: exactly one token leg, the token the rebate is paid in, amount above 0.

rewardKind.description: Optional "DIRECT": the payout pays tokens. Leaving it out means the same.

rebatePercent.description: The percent of each wallet's metric paid back, above 0 and at most 100. The rebate is paid in the pool's token, so the metric should be in that token's units.

rebateStrategy.description: What happens when the pool cannot pay every rebate. "PRIORITIZE_TOP": the highest metrics are paid in full until the pool runs out. "PRORATE": every rebate is scaled down by the same share.

anyOf.description: REBATE paying tokens: a one-token pool, the percent paid back, and what happens when the pool runs short.

totalFundAmount.description: The pool it pays from, per epoch on an EPOCH incentive: one token leg per token, each amount above 0. Every token a prize pays needs a pool here, and every pool here must be one of the tokens it pays.

rewardKind.description: Optional "DIRECT": the payout pays tokens. Leaving it out means the same.

selectionLogic.description: "EQUAL_CHANCES": every wallet the query returns has one ticket. "WEIGHTED_BY_METRIC": a wallet's tickets are its metric, so the query needs a metric column.

allowDuplicateWinners.description: Whether one wallet can win more than one prize.

prizeBuckets.description: The prizes. Each `{amount, count}` pays `count` winners `amount` each, where `amount` is a list of token legs. A token's prizes may total no more than its pool.

anyOf.description: RAFFLE paying tokens: a pool, how tickets are counted, and the prizes.

rewardKind.description: "CRATE": the payout pays crates instead of tokens.

anyOf.description: RAFFLE paying crates (rewardKind "CRATE"): every wallet the query returns earns one crate while stock lasts, drawn from `crateInventory`; the RAFFLE fields for tokens are not used.

totalFundAmount.description: The pool it pays from, per epoch on an EPOCH incentive: one token leg per token, each amount above 0. Every token the reward pays needs a pool here, and every pool here must be one of the tokens it pays. Once a pool runs out, the wallets left are not paid.

rewardKind.description: Optional "DIRECT": the payout pays tokens. Leaving it out means the same.

participantReward.description: What every wallet the query returns is paid: a list of token legs.

anyOf.description: FIXED paying tokens: a pool and the reward every wallet gets.

rewardKind.description: "CRATE": the payout pays crates instead of tokens.

anyOf.description: FIXED paying crates (rewardKind "CRATE"): every wallet the query returns earns one crate while stock lasts, drawn from `crateInventory`; the FIXED fields for tokens are not used.

distributionConfig.description: The payout's settings, in a shape of `payoutType`: paying tokens, or for LEADERBOARD, RAFFLE or FIXED paying crates (`rewardKind: "CRATE"`).

instructions:
Use the Torque DSL (a JSON spec the API runs) for data questions. Never write SQL.

Data questions (volume, traders, counts, events, trends, breakdowns, top wallets by a raw measure; for an incentive's own ranking or scores use `get_incentive_leaderboard`):
1. Call `get_metrics` (`incentiveId` for one incentive); if a saved metric answers, read it with `values: true`. A metric's value covers the incentive's whole window or one epoch; for any other window, run its `spec` from `get_metrics` with `run_query` and `start`/`end`.
2. Else read `get_dsl_guide` (default, then `section: "catalog"`) once per project; `section: "examples"` has patterns, and for one incentive read it with its `incentiveId`.
3. Run it with `run_query`; fix a failure from its message; after 3 tries, ask the user.
4. Give the numbers, the window and, for one incentive, which wallets they cover; if `run_query` says metric-ready, offer `save_metric`.
5. If part needs a definition or has no data, keep the population asked about: state a default, answer the rest, label the gap, offer to refine. If no tool reads it, say so first; name any other population in the same sentence as its numbers.

Create a metric: check `get_metrics`, run the spec, then `save_metric`; it previews, then saves on a repeat with its token once the user approves.
Create an incentive (DSL only, never SQL): run the spec with `run_query`, then `create_incentive`; it previews, then creates on a repeat with its token once the user approves. Prompt: `create-incentive`.

Fixed facts, not queries: `get_incentive_analytics` (one incentive's funded, allocated and claimed amounts to date, its epochs, emissions, funding events and crate counts), `get_incentive_leaderboard` and `get_rewards` (rewards counted in a window, per incentive, with their cost). The first two also read a granted incentive.
Who qualifies, or how wallets score: the qualification query in `get_incentive`.
Examples: `torque://dsl/usage`.
